title: tighten-ingress-routing-payload-clamping-and-stream-buffer-safeguards
author: Priya Raman
body: Context and motivation: We have seen intermittent customer reports where long-running streaming sessions with fncall/tool calls produce corrupted structured-output boundaries or stall during the handshake when routed through busy gateway instances. Root cause analysis pointed to two contributing factors: (1) aggressive route-level payload allowances that allowed oversized control frames to bypass stream backpressure logic, and (2) a proxy coalescing window that could over-aggregate small fragments causing the fncall newline/JSON boundary detector to miss delimiters under head-of-line conditions. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a per-route soft-clamp for declared payloads and an enforced hard-cap at the gateway ingress. Soft-clamp emits telemetry and reduces credit assignment; hard-cap returns a clear 413-like OpenAI-compat error with structured JSON error body to preserve clients expecting OpenAI semantics. 2) Add a streaming proxy buffer TTL and minimum flush thresholds so fragments are not held indefinitely to wait for aggregation; this reduces boundary-detection stalls for function/toolcall handshakes. 3) Modify routing rules: small-payload preferential steering sends sub-4KB control/tool frames to low-latency worker pools; large payloads follow capacity-aware routing paths. 4) Update OpenAI compatibility layer adapter to normalize error shape for the new hard-cap and to retry a single-time route fallback to a compatible model variant (if available) when a payload is blocked due to capacity gating. 5) Add an explicit structured-output delimiter verifier that runs on stream flush to detect truncated JSON/NDJSON and surface clearer evalable errors. Implementation notes and trade-offs: The soft-clamp emits a new metric gateway.route_payload_soft_clamp{route,customer} which is used by Optimize suggestions; we kept the soft behavior conservative to avoid false positives. The hard-cap is intentionally strict to make client behavior deterministic and to enable backend autoscaling signals when customers repeatedly hit the cap. Buffer TTL is default 75ms (configurable) with an opt-out per-route for legacy customers who require maximal merge coalescing. Routing heuristics use request metadata (content-length hints, control-frame flag, and prior tail-latency samples) to pick a target worker pool; this adds an extra routing decision but reduces end-to-end fncall latency on observed workloads. Tests and safety: Unit and integration tests added: gateway/router_test.go (route selection and clamp enforcement), gateway/stream_proxy_test.go (buffer TTL and flush thresholds), compat/openai/adapter_test.go (error normalization and retry path). We exercised a canary rollout: 10% of traffic in us-west1 for 48 hours with synthetic fncall scenarios and incremental increase to 50% after observing no regressions. Backwards compatibility and rollout plan: Default behavior is backward compatible due to soft-clamp telemetry enabling and the hard-cap only triggering on oversized payloads. Customers who relied on previous implicit coalescing can opt out with a per-route annotation to restore previous buffer behavior for 30 days while they migrate. Docs and observability: Added docs/compatibility/openai.md section documenting the new 413 structured error and suggested client retry/backoff behavior. New Grafana panels for route_payload_soft_clamp and proxy_fragment_ttl_expiry were introduced and wired to the Console. Commit summary: - commit 1: gateway: add per-route soft-clamp and hard-cap enforcement with metrics emission - commit 2: stream proxy: implement TTL and min-flush threshold, add unit tests - commit 3: openai-compat: normalize hard-cap error shape and implement single-fallback routing - commit 4: sdk/python: update streaming client docstring to mention structured error handling - commit 5: docs: add compatibility notes and rollout instructions Files changed (high level): - gateway/router.go: routing decision heuristics and route annotation parsing - gateway/payload_limits.go: soft-clamp/hard-cap logic and metrics - gateway/stream_proxy.go: buffer TTL, flush thresholds, and fragment coalescer tuning - compat/openai/adapter.go: error normalization and fallback routing - sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py: client handling note and small compatibility helper - docs/compatibility/openai.md: docs for new behavior - tests/integration/streaming_toolcall_test.go: e2e scenarios and regression checks Review conversation summary: - Ethan Morales (reviewer): "Please add a short circuit for health-check traffic so the new routing heuristics don't add latency to probes." Author reply: "Added a navigator health-check bypass in router.go; updated tests to assert zero added latency." - Lina Gupta: "Can the buffer TTL be exposed as a per-customer override in the Console?" Author reply: "Planned: added backlog task in ENG-4321 to wire Console toggle; default behavior stays server-side for safety." - Marcus Lee: "OpenAI error shape change may break older clients; ensure we include a clear migration note in release notes." Author reply: "Added compatibility docs and included an example of runtime-decoding that falls back to the older shape if needed." CI and validation: - CI: build: passed - CI: unit tests: initial run failed (flaky coalescer test); rerun passed - CI: integration (streaming): passed - Load test: local run against staging clusters showed 1.8% p95 latency improvement for fncall scenarios and a 0.7% increase in gateway CPU due to lightweight routing heuristics Observability notes: - New metrics: gateway.route_payload_soft_clamp (counter), gateway.route_payload_hard_cap (counter), proxy.fragment_ttl_expiry (counter) - Alerts: created a warning alert for repeated hard-cap hits per customer (linked to support playbook) Merge and rollout outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-20 after approvals from all reviewers and green CI. Gradual rollout to production with canary gates at 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100% over 72 hours. Release notes: - Improve streaming stability for function/toolcall handshakes by reducing fragment aggregation stalls and adding explicit structured-output verification. - Add per-route payload soft-clamp telemetry and a hard-cap that returns OpenAI-compatible structured errors for oversized payloads. - Introduce buffer TTL on the streaming proxy to reduce boundary detection stalls. - Prefer low-latency worker pools for small control/tool frames to reduce fncall tail latency. - New metrics and console panels for monitoring route payloads and proxy TTL expiries.
